title: Lionel Hampton and the xylophone
summary: Hinton adds Lionel Hampton; Jones says he got Hampton xylophones for speed and advised him to follow Red Norvo.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: It's very difficult to recall in any given

time all the very great people who so justly deserve to be mentioned. In doing this we've left out one of the most financially successful and certainly one of the great innovators of jazz drumming. It's just an oversight on my part because we know him as a big band leader. We just forget to mention Lionel Hampton. the great Hump?
Let's leave him with his telephones. Lionel Hampton sit down there with them telephones, those vibraphones. That's it. Telephones. H: Is that what you call them? Jones': Telephones.
I remember back in Chicago, we played in Chicago in the Defender band together. I've seen him come a long ways and I thought maybe we could -

No, Lionel - you got to sacrifice something, so he went to the vibes and the sensational things that he got to. When he was with Benny I used to go down to the Paramount Theatre, because I remember I got him a set of xylophones, because xylophones is fast. Vibraphones are slow with electronics. That gave him his speed, so naturally when he'd practice on those and go to the vibraphones it was not too difficult. He hadn't met Red Norvo, you see. I said, get with Red Norvo. Red Norvo played the xylophones; Red didn't play vibraphones. That's the reason Red's speed didn't make no difference. So I said, "Get you about 6 things that you do, Lionel. Cut out a whole lot of things." It's the same way that I used to do with Sid Catlett. We used to sit down and rehearse different things that I couldn't
do in Basie's band. I couldn't afford to throw those sticks up in the air and running around the room and beating on no drums.
